communityVoices.quote: At this point, Slipknot! is actually more of a free jam more than a true Slipknot - and a helluva jam at that.
Is this the best version of Crazy Fingers? Maybe, maybe not. All I know is Garcia still can sing it here in '76.
The Jam in the middle is flawless and the Jam into Dancin' is golden.
I don't know if I've heard another show where every single band member was having such an incredible night all at once.
the 76 summer tour was gaining speed JG and the band boogie away into the morning Alchemy

whyThisShow: This is the first of two nights at the Beacon Theatre on the return from the '75 hiatus, and one reviewer calls it "the more extraordinary, overall" of the pair. The show has been officially released, and the soundboard source is described as having "pure and exceptional" quality with "the mix is perfect, clarity right on and no background hiss". One listener notes it used to appear "on all-time-best lists during B&P trading" but has since become "something of a hidden gem". The consensus pull is the second set, anchored by a Crazy Fingers, Help/Slip/Frank sequence, and a Cosmic Charlie that one listener calls "the neatliest" of the post-hiatus returns.
listenFor: The Crazy Fingers is the song most reviewers flag first — one calls the "instrumental jam at the end" "so hypnotic", while another says it goes "into a Spanish-Jam-ish before a drum segue into Dancin'". The Slipknot! is worth particular attention: one listener says it is "actually more of a free jam more than a true Slipknot" and credits it as one of the highlights of the night. One reviewer singles out the Slipknot!–Franklin's Tower transition as potentially "the best ever," describing it as "a great example of how 'out there' they could get without losing each other". On the source side, one reviewer notes that "only the hollister_22804 is complete, and is the best source from High Time onward".
context: This show comes from the summer 1976 tour, the band's first full return to touring after the extended 1975 hiatus. It was one of only two nights the Dead ever played the Beacon Theatre on the upper west side, a room that seated roughly 2,800. The show has been officially released as 'Beacon Theatre, New York, NY 6/14/76.' The best complete recording is the SBD identifier gd76-06-14.sbd.hollister.22804.sbeok.shnf; one reviewer notes the alternate sirmick matrix has cuts in High Time and Franklin's Tower. One listener flags that it was Phil Lesh's birthday and speculates "he's using a fretless bass".
funFact: One reviewer notes that the Might as Well performed here was only "the 5th airing and now ready to amaze," calling it part of "a helluva sequence".
headline: Phil's birthday at the Beacon, June '76.
